article.name: AgentWorkingMemory
article.summary: AgentWorkingMemory (AWM) is a local-first agent memory application with selective writes, multi-stage retrieval, correction and retraction flows, and local or server database backends. This is a source review, not a runtime or performance assessment.

who_what.text: The official repository README describes AgentWorkingMemory as a local-first AI-agent memory application distributed as a Node.js package with MCP, HTTP, CLI, and Claude Code integration surfaces. This review makes no individual maintainer claim.

architecture.text: The architecture guide describes MCP and HTTP entry points over shared cognitive engines and SQLite/FTS5 storage. The MCP entry point registers memory and task tools and starts a hook sidecar; the guide says the MCP and HTTP entry points are not designed to run simultaneously against one database.

The engram schema includes agent ID, concept, content, tags, type/class, salience, confidence, access state, embedding and lifecycle stage; optional validity, question, slot, task and origin fields are also described. Associations connect engrams and episodes group related items.
The default backend is SQLite with FTS5, WAL and a slim in-memory cache; the architecture guide also describes PGlite and Postgres backends. Backend parity and production behavior were not tested.

behavior.text: Write uses the shared pipeline to redact configured sensitive patterns, evaluate novelty and salience, and create, reinforce an exact-concept match, or supersede a prior item under correction rules. Some low-salience writes are staged or discarded; embedding and connection work may continue asynchronously.

Supersession creates a replacement engram and marks the prior one superseded. Retraction is a soft invalidation path: it can create a correction and invalidation edge and lower confidence in a bounded set of connected memories. A general hard-delete tool was not identified in the inspected MCP surface.

Retrieval embeds the query, obtains lexical and vector candidates, computes text/confidence/decay/association signals, walks graph links, reranks a bounded pool with a local cross-encoder, applies validity/supersession and agreement rules, and returns a limited result. Some calibrated abstention behavior is opt-in.

The schema and entry point expose activation events, retrieval feedback, staging events, structured logs and loop-lag monitoring. These are instrumentation paths, not measured results from this review.

metrics.evidence: Multi-stage retrieval and agreement or optional calibrated gates are visible in code; no adjudicated answerable or unsupported probes were run.
Supersession, validity windows and retraction mechanisms exist; no correction or stale-value workload was measured.
Retraction marks a record invalid without hard deletion; the reviewed MCP surface did not establish general permanent-erasure coverage.
Agent and session identifiers are used in memory flows, but this review did not test API authorization or cross-scope leakage.
Origin and reference fields preserve some context, but a required validated evidence chain was not established.
Parallel lexical/vector retrieval, local model scoring, and event latency fields are visible; no workload timings were collected.
Local models, SQLite configuration, and token/context helpers are present; no task-specific token, cost, or storage measurements were taken.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected documentation and source at one verified repository head. It did not establish runtime correctness, retrieval quality, deletion completeness, authorization, production reliability, or measured resource use.
The repository documents multiple storage backends and configurable paths. Backend parity, every route-level scope check, lifecycle edge cases, and maintenance effects were not exhaustively audited.
The checked official README did not publish a contact email. The contact record stores null and the exact checked README source URL; no address was inferred.
The curated roster and its pinned Atlas locator supplied ordinal, name, repository locator, and source attribution only; Atlas assessment descriptions, marks, and layout were excluded.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status: not run for AgentWorkingMemory in this task. The project's metric definitions, status record, and planned fixture are separate from these source findings. No system execution, benchmark, or tests were run.
